use_when: At the end of a dialog or form, to pair the main action with a way out, such as "Publish review" and "Save as draft", or "Save role and access" and "Cancel".
Use type destructive when the main action deletes or cancels something, such as "Continue to cancel" and "Keep my booking".
Use type secondary for two actions of equal weight, such as "View" and "Modify" on a trip card.
Use layout stack on narrow screens such as the mobile app, with the main action on top.
Use type segmented to switch a view between 2 to 4 options, such as the time range "Last 24 hours / 7 days / 30 days / Custom range" on the back office dashboard. Exactly one segment is selected.

dont_use_when.when: For a single action: use the Button component instead.
To filter a list by several values at once: use the Chip component instead. Segments pick exactly one option.
For more than three actions, or more than four segments: move the extras into a Dropdown component.

variant_intent.segmented: segmented (2 to 4 options, one selected in navy, the rest outlined; row only)
variant_intent.row: row (default, main action on the left)
variant_intent.stack: stack (full width, main action on top; not for segmented)

a11y.fact: The button types render a role="group" container; callers name it with aria-label (spread onto the div).
The button types compose the native Button, so each action is a real <button> with its visible text as its accessible name.
The segmented type renders a role="radiogroup" container; callers name it with aria-label.
Each segment is a native <input type="radio"> inside a <label>, all sharing one name, so exactly one is selected and arrow-key behaviour is the browser's own; aria-pressed is not used.
The radio input is transparent (not display:none), so it stays focusable and exposed to assistive technology while the label draws the segment.
Keyboard focus on a segment shows the browser's native focus ring on its label, via :has(input:focus-visible).
